name: Fake field goal
seenIn: Covered in Football 101, Lesson 61: The fake field goal: when the holder and kicker become a backfield (and how Oregon scored before halftime)
what: A fake field goal is a trick play run out of the field-goal formation. Everything looks like a kick: the long snapper, the holder kneeling about 7 yards back and the kicker lining up his approach. But instead of setting the ball down, the holder keeps it.

From there the holder can run, throw to a wing or tight end who slips out, or pitch it to the kicker, who is already moving forward. It works because the defense sends 9 or more players up the middle to block the kick, so the outside is nearly empty, and nobody is assigned to tackle the kicker.

Coaches call it when film shows a weak spot in how a team defends kicks, often on 4th-and-short or right before halftime. It is a gamble: if it works, 3 points become 7 (or a fresh set of downs); if it fails, the team gets nothing and gives the ball away.

caption: Dashed white: the snap to the holder (H) and his pitch to the kicker (K). Solid white: the kicker's run around the edge. Yellow dashes: the edge rushers charging in to block the kick and the lone cornerback coming up too late.
spot: It starts as a normal field-goal try. The giveaway is the holder standing up with the ball instead of placing it, then running, throwing or pitching it to the kicker. Watch for clues before the snap: 4th-and-short, a wing lined up wider than usual, a backup QB as the holder, or a defense with only 10 players or everyone rushing inside.
beats: Defenses that load everyone inside to block the kick and leave the edges empty. Log it as Run in the drill when the holder runs or pitches, or Pass if he throws.
